nodes.name: Weekly Cron (Friday 5pm)
nodes.notes: Fires every Friday at 17:00. Edit triggerAtHour / triggerAtDay to change schedule.

nodes.name: Fetch Merged PRs
nodes.notes: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=closed — filtered to merged_at in Code node

nodes.name: Set Config Variables
nodes.notes: Reads GITHUB_OWNER, GITHUB_REPO, SUMMARY_LANG from environment variables (with defaults). Computes the 'since' date (7 days ago).

nodes.name: Aggregate & Format Data
nodes.notes: Combines outputs from all three GitHub API calls. Filters merged PRs by date, removes PRs from issues list, truncates for large repos, detects empty weeks.

nodes.name: Empty Week?
nodes.notes: Routes to a static 'no activity' message if the week had zero commits, issues, and PRs.

nodes.name: Empty Week Message
nodes.notes: Generates a static message when no GitHub activity was found for the week.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514', max_tokens: 2048, messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'You are a senior developer writing a weekly development summary for a team channel (Discord/Slack). Write in ' + $json.language + ' language (EN=English, FR=French).

Repository: ' + $json.repo + '
Period: ' + $json.weekStart + ' to ' + $json.weekEnd + '

RAW DATA:

## Commits (' + $json.stats.totalCommits + ' total)
' + JSON.stringify($json.commits, null, 2) + '

## Closed Issues (' + $json.stats.closedIssues + ' total)
' + JSON.stringify($json.closedIssues, null, 2) + '

## Merged PRs (' + $json.stats.mergedPRs + ' total)
' + JSON.stringify($json.mergedPRs, null, 2) + '

## Contributors: ' + $json.contributors.join(', ') + ($json.wasTruncated ? '

Note: Data was truncated due to volume. Summarize based on available data and note there was more.' : '') + '

---
INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Start with a header: "## 📊 Weekly Dev Summary — {repo}" and the date range.
2. Write a 2-3 sentence executive summary of the week's highlights.
3. Section: "🔨 Key Changes" — group related commits into themes (max 5 themes). Mention notable commit authors.
4. Section: "✅ Issues Resolved" — list closed issues, grouped by label/category if possible.
5. Section: "🔀 Pull Requests Merged" — highlight the most impactful PRs with authors.
6. Section: "👥 Contributors" — shout out active contributors.
7. Section: "📈 Stats" — show commit count, issues closed, PRs merged, contributor count.
8. End with a brief forward-looking note or team encouragement.

Format for Discord/Slack markdown. Keep it concise but informative. Use emoji for visual appeal. Maximum 1500 characters.' }] }) }}

nodes.name: Claude Summarize
nodes.notes: Calls Claude claude-sonnet-4-20250514 to generate a narrative summary from the raw GitHub data. The prompt instructs Claude to format for Discord/Slack with sections, emoji, and stats.

nodes.name: Extract & Fallback
nodes.notes: Extracts the text from Claude's response. If Claude returns an error, builds a fallback summary from raw stats. Truncates to fit Discord's 2000-char message limit.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ content: $json.summary, username: 'Dev Summary Bot', avatar_url: 'https://github.githubassets.com/images/modules/logos_page/GitHub-Mark.png' }) }}

nodes.name: Send to Discord
nodes.notes: Posts the summary to a Discord channel via webhook. Set DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL env var or edit the URL directly. For Slack: change URL to Slack webhook and body to { "text": $json.summary }.

nodes.name: Log Result
nodes.notes: Final node — logs delivery status for execution history.

nodes.name: Error Handler
nodes.notes: Catches unhandled errors. Connected as error trigger output.
